difficultyReason: Simple two-fact conflict with one obvious confounder: park attendance fell despite expansion. Correct answer identifies a competing attraction opened simultaneously. Only one choice addresses both horns.
stimulus: Riverside Park expanded its facilities by 40 percent last year, yet attendance actually declined by 15 percent. However, a new entertainment complex opened two blocks away the same month the park's expansion was completed.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Riverside Park raised its admission fee by 10 percent when the expansion was completed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new entertainment complex offered free admission during its first three months of operation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The park's new facilities were not yet fully operational at the time of the attendance measurement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other parks in the region reported stable attendance figures during the same period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The park's original facilities remained open and functional throughout the expansion project.

explanations.correct: If the new entertainment complex offered free admission, this explains why people visited it instead of the expanded park, even though the park expanded. Both facts—expansion and attendance decline—are now reconciled by competition from the free alternative.
explanations.A: A fee increase would explain the attendance decline, but it doesn't explain why the park expanded in the first place, leaving the scenario still counterintuitive.
explanations.C: Operational delays would explain lower attendance but don't resolve why the park bothered expanding immediately, and doesn't touch the real cause.
explanations.D: Other parks' stability doesn't explain why this park's attendance fell despite its own improvements.
explanations.E: Keeping original facilities operational is irrelevant to the conflict between expansion and declining attendance.

stimulus_note: Two-part stimulus: (1) park expanded 40%, (2) attendance declined 15%. Stimulus triggers paradox structure.

difficultyReason: Straightforward medical case: drug reduces symptom severity yet doesn't improve patient outcomes. Correct answer identifies that patients stop taking drug early because symptoms improve, leaving underlying condition untreated. Single obvious mechanism resolves both facts.
stimulus: A new antifever medication reduces fever severity in 85 percent of patients who take it, yet clinical trials show it does not improve overall patient recovery rates. Despite this, doctors continue to prescribe it.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The medication has fewer side effects than older fever-reducing drugs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients often stop taking the medication once their fever subsides, before the underlying infection is fully resolved.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fever is a symptom that naturally subsides over time in most patients.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The medication works by stimulating the immune system rather than by lowering body temperature.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insurance companies readily cover the cost of this medication.

explanations.correct: If patients quit taking the medication as soon as symptoms improve, they interrupt the course of treatment before the underlying infection is cured. This explains why symptom relief doesn't translate to better outcomes—the medication works, but patients stop prematurely.
explanations.A: Fewer side effects explains why doctors prefer it, but doesn't reconcile the symptom relief vs. no-outcome-improvement paradox.
explanations.C: If fever subsides naturally, this would question why the medication gets credit for symptom relief at all, deepening rather than resolving the paradox.
explanations.D: The mechanism of action doesn't explain why symptom relief doesn't improve recovery.
explanations.E: Insurance coverage is irrelevant to the symptom relief vs. patient outcomes conflict.

stimulus_note: Medication reduces fever severity (85%) but doesn't improve recovery outcomes. Doctors still prescribe. Paradox structure is clear.

difficultyReason: Economics domain: handmade goods priced higher than mass-produced alternatives, yet handmade market is growing. Correct answer identifies luxury/status signal mechanism. Clear single confounder.
stimulus: Handmade pottery sells for three times the price of machine-produced pottery, yet sales of handmade pottery have increased 35 percent in the past two years. Machine-produced pottery sales have remained flat.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Machine-produced pottery is sold in more retail locations than handmade pottery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consumers increasingly view handmade goods as status symbols and are willing to pay premiums for them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The prices of both handmade and machine-produced pottery have risen over the past two years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Handmade pottery is more durable than machine-produced pottery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mass production has become more efficient, lowering the cost of machine-produced pottery.

explanations.correct: If handmade goods are now valued as status symbols, higher prices no longer deter purchase—they actually attract buyers seeking exclusivity and prestige. This explains why raising prices coincides with growing sales.
explanations.A: Distribution differences don't explain why higher prices drive growth in handmade sales.
explanations.C: Price increases apply to both categories, so this doesn't explain why handmade sales grew while machine-produced sales stagnated.
explanations.D: Superior durability might justify higher prices but doesn't explain why sales grew despite the price premium.
explanations.E: Lower machine-produced prices would make the flat sales even more paradoxical, not less.

stimulus_note: Handmade pottery is 3x more expensive yet sales grew 35%. Contrast setup is explicit.

difficultyReason: Environmental science: conservation effort preserves species yet total wild population stable. Correct answer identifies that without effort, population would have crashed. Obvious temporal/counterfactual logic.
stimulus: An endangered bird species was protected through strict hunting bans and habitat restoration spanning twelve years. Yet the species' total population in the wild has remained stable rather than increasing noticeably.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The bird species reproduces slowly and only reaches sexual maturity after five years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Without the hunting bans and habitat restoration, the species would have become extinct within the same twelve-year period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Other endangered bird species in the same region have shown population increases after similar conservation efforts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bird species has no natural predators in its habitat.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Illegal hunting of the species continues in remote areas despite the official ban.

explanations.correct: If the population would have crashed without intervention, maintaining stability is actually a conservation success. The paradox dissolves when we recognize that 'no growth' in the context of prevention is not a failure.
explanations.A: Slow reproduction explains why growth is slow, but doesn't reconcile why a costly, multi-year effort produced no noticeable gains.
explanations.C: Other species' success doesn't explain this species' lack of growth.
explanations.D: Absence of predators doesn't explain why strict protection didn't yield population increases.
explanations.E: Ongoing poaching would actually explain the lack of growth, but this makes the story worse, not better resolved.

stimulus_note: Strict 12-year conservation effort on endangered bird, yet stable (not growing) population. Paradox about effort and outcome.

difficultyReason: Technology domain: tech company acquired for high price yet posted losses. Correct answer identifies acquisition valued intellectual property/patents, not current earnings. Single, obvious mechanism.
stimulus: A technology startup was acquired by a major corporation for 500 million dollars, yet the startup had posted significant financial losses in each of the three years prior to acquisition.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Technology startups typically operate at a loss during their first five years of operation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The acquiring corporation anticipated that the startup's patents and technology would generate substantial future revenues.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The startup had been founded by engineers who previously worked at the acquiring corporation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The technology sector experienced rapid growth in the years immediately preceding the acquisition.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Other startups in the same field were acquired at lower prices during the same period.

explanations.correct: If the acquirer valued the startup's intellectual property and future potential rather than its current earnings, the high acquisition price makes sense despite losses. The price reflects future value, not past performance.
explanations.A: That startups commonly run at a loss explains the pattern generally but doesn't explain why this specific unprofitable startup commanded such a high price.
explanations.C: The founders' history doesn't explain the valuation premium.
explanations.D: Sector growth might encourage acquisitions generally but doesn't explain why losses don't reduce valuation.
explanations.E: Other companies' prices don't explain this company's valuation.

stimulus_note: Startup with 3-year losses acquired for $500M. Paradox: why pay so much for a losing company?

difficultyReason: History/policy: law intended to increase voter participation yet voter turnout declined in following election. Correct answer identifies confounding factor (competing election distraction). Single clear mechanism.
stimulus: A state legislature passed a law making voter registration simpler and more accessible. Yet in the election held immediately after the law took effect, voter turnout in that state decreased by 5 percent compared to the previous election.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to explain the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The state legislature also passed laws reducing the length of the voting period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The previous election had coincided with a highly contested gubernatorial race, while the subsequent election involved primarily local and state legislative races.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Voter registration has been shown to increase voter participation in some states but not others.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The new registration law was passed by the state legislature only weeks before the election.

choices.label: E
choices.text: In neighboring states, voter turnout also declined during the same election cycle.

explanations.correct: If the previous election featured a high-stakes gubernatorial race while the subsequent one did not, the lower turnout reflects reduced voter interest in the contest, not a failure of registration reform. The easier registration couldn't overcome voter apathy toward less prominent races.
explanations.A: Voting period restrictions would explain lower turnout directly, but this contradicts the stimulus's assumption that registration was the intended driver.
explanations.C: That registration helps in some states but not others is too vague and doesn't resolve the specific paradox here.
explanations.D: Late passage explains why registration uptake might be slow, but doesn't directly reconcile the turnout decline.
explanations.E: Regional turnout patterns don't explain the state-specific paradox.

stimulus_note: Law simplifying registration passed, yet turnout declined in next election. Paradox structure clear.

difficultyReason: Linguistics: new grammar rule taught in schools yet standardized test scores declined. Correct answer identifies that scores measure older writing standard, creating temporal mismatch. Single obvious resolution.
stimulus: A school district implemented a new grammar curriculum emphasizing clearer sentence structure, yet student performance on standardized writing tests declined by 8 percent in the year following implementation.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new curriculum required students to learn significantly more grammar rules than the previous curriculum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The standardized test had not been updated in ten years and continued to assess writing skills according to older grammatical standards.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Student writing improved in other measures such as paragraph organization and use of evidence.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The new curriculum was developed by linguists with expertise in sentence composition.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Other school districts that implemented the same curriculum also saw declining test scores.

explanations.correct: If the test hasn't been updated and measures an older standard, the new curriculum's improved structure might conflict with what the outdated test assesses. Students taught the new way perform worse on a test designed for the old way—a measurement mismatch, not a curriculum failure.
explanations.A: Learning more rules might explain why scores dipped initially, but this doesn't resolve the paradox; it deepens it.
explanations.C: Improvements in other areas don't explain why the tested measure declined.
explanations.D: Expert development doesn't explain poor test performance.
explanations.E: Other districts' results don't explain the local paradox.

stimulus_note: New grammar curriculum emphasizing clarity, yet writing test scores declined. Paradox stem present.

difficultyReason: Ethics/law: company's ethical code expanded yet employee ethics complaints increased. Correct answer identifies that expanded code awareness enables more complaints to be filed. Single obvious mechanism.
stimulus: A corporation revised its ethics code to be more comprehensive and established a new confidential complaint hotline. Yet the number of ethics violations reported by employees nearly tripled in the following year.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The corporation's profits declined significantly during the year following the ethics code revision.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Employees who previously feared retaliation for reporting violations were now confident that the anonymous hotline would protect their identity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ethics violations in the corporation's industry increased overall during the same time period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The corporation hired a new chief ethics officer to oversee compliance with the code.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Other corporations in the industry did not establish confidential complaint mechanisms.

explanations.correct: If employees were previously afraid to report violations but now feel protected by anonymity, the tripling of reports reflects not an increase in actual violations but an increase in *reporting* of pre-existing violations. The ethics code enabled disclosure, not misconduct.
explanations.A: Profit decline might explain increased unethical behavior, but doesn't address why a better code and safer reporting channel would increase complaints.
explanations.C: Industry-wide increase doesn't explain why this specific corporation's reported violations tripled after policy changes.
explanations.D: A new officer might oversee code enforcement but doesn't explain why violations nearly tripled specifically after the changes.
explanations.E: Competitors' lack of mechanisms doesn't explain this corporation's reported increase.

stimulus_note: Comprehensive ethics code and anonymous hotline established, yet ethics complaints tripled. Paradox stem clear.
